content.en: Notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, replacing the 2000 rules, extending the territorial jurisdiction beyond municipal areas to outgrowths, census towns, defense establishments, and religious hubs.
content.hi: Notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, replacing the 2000 rules, extending the territorial jurisdiction beyond municipal areas to outgrowths, census towns, defense establishments, and religious hubs.

content.en:
1. Segregation at Source into three streams: Wet (Biodegradable), Dry (Recyclable), and Domestic Hazardous waste.
2. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for packaging brand owners.
3. Integration of informal waste pickers and ragpickers into formal collection systems.
4. Mandatory usage of Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) in cement kilns within 100 km.
5. Spot fines for littering and "user fee" collection by local bodies.
content.hi:
1. Segregation at Source into three streams: Wet (Biodegradable), Dry (Recyclable), and Domestic Hazardous waste.

4. Mandatory usage of Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) in cement kilns within 100 km.
5. Spot fines for littering and "user fee" collection by local bodies.

question.en: According to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, waste generators must segregate waste at source into how many distinct streams?
question.hi: According to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, waste generators must segregate waste at source into how many distinct streams?

text.en: Three streams (Biodegradable, Dry/Recyclable, and Domestic Hazardous)
text.hi: Three streams (Biodegradable, Dry/Recyclable, and Domestic Hazardous)

explanation.en: Rule 4 mandates segregation at source into three streams: Biodegradable (Wet waste), Non-biodegradable (Dry waste), and Domestic Hazardous waste (sanitary napkins, diapers, batteries, insect sprays).
explanation.hi: Rule 4 mandates segregation at source into three streams: Biodegradable (Wet waste), Non-biodegradable (Dry waste), and Domestic Hazardous waste (sanitary napkins, diapers, batteries, insect sprays).
